title: Limited prescribing authority in a community pharmacy: extension, dosage actions, disease states and co-morbidities
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.03(5)(e)1., an authorized pharmacist currently registered by the Department, pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 7 and 9 and 105 CMR 700.000, to prescribe and possess controlled substances, who practices in a community pharmacy pursuant to a collaborative practice agreement that includes individually developed prescriptive practice guidelines pursuant to which the supervising physician has authorized the pharmacist to prescribe, may: a. extend current drug therapy by 30 days for not more than two 30 day periods or as may otherwise be specifically authorized by the supervising physician in the referral of the patient and as provided in the CDTM agreement; and b. initiate, modify or discontinue dosages of medications prescribed by the supervising physician for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, congestive heart failure, HIV or AIDS, osteoporosis, and co-morbidities listed in i. through viii. and identified by the supervising physician along with the primary diagnosis in the supervising physician's referral of the patient. 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)6.a. and b. state the same authority.
exam_relevance: Tests the regulatory limits on what a community pharmacist may do under the agreement, and where they differ in words from the statutory retail limb: the number of 30-day extensions, the verbs initiate and discontinue, and co-morbidities confined to the eight listed conditions.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations
Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

numeric_facts.fact: Length of each extension of current drug therapy
Number of 30-day extension periods, unless otherwise specifically authorized by the supervising physician in the referral and as provided in the agreement
numeric_facts.conditions: not more than two 30 day periods

exceptions: The two-period limit on extensions yields where a longer extension is otherwise specifically authorized by the supervising physician in the referral of the patient and as provided in the CDTM agreement.
common_confusions: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5) speaks of an extension by 30 days and of the modification of dosages; the regulations speak of not more than two 30 day periods and of initiating, modifying or discontinuing dosages.

The statute reaches co-morbidities identified by the supervising physician for the individual patient along with the primary diagnosis; the regulations reach co-morbidities listed among the eight named conditions and identified by the supervising physician along with the primary diagnosis in the referral.

The authority is conditioned on a current Department registration to prescribe and possess controlled substances and on an agreement with individually developed prescriptive practice guidelines under which the supervising physician has authorized the pharmacist to prescribe.
verification_notes: Read in the current mass.gov PDF of 247 CMR 16.00 (regulation page dated 12/15/2017) and in the current mass.gov PDF of 243 CMR 2.00 on 2026-09-17, and compared with the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5) on malegislature.gov.
